name: Abū ʿAlī Ismāʿīl ibn al-Qāsim ibn ʿAydhūn al-Qālī al-Baghdādī
summary: Baghdad-trained lexicographer and grammarian who brought the learning of Iraq to Cordoba; author of al-Amālī and teacher of al-Zubaydī.
bio: Al-Qālī was born in Manāzgird in Armenia in 288/901 and studied for more than twenty years in Baghdad, with Ibn Durayd, Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī, al-Zajjāj, Nifṭawayh and Ibn Durustawayh. In 330/942 he went to al-Andalus at the invitation of the Umayyad court and taught in Cordoba until his death in 356/967.

He brought with him the books and chains of transmission of the Iraqi grammarians and lexicographers. His al-Amālī, dictated in the mosque of Cordoba, is a classic of Arabic letters, and his dictionary al-Bāriʿ followed al-Khalīl's order. Al-Zubaydī was his student and opens the Ṭabaqāt with a chain that begins 'Abū ʿAlī al-Qālī said'; he lists his teacher twice, among the Basran grammarians of the tenth generation and among the lexicographers.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 55 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
